summary: gd-quadratic: sliders for eta (0.01-2.5, log, default 1.8, ticks at 1 and 2), kappa (1-1000, log, default 20), sigma_g (0-1, default 0); preset dropdown (6 presets + custom); Run/Step/Reset; click on contours sets w0. Default state shows the zig-zag: steep factor -0.800, flat 0.910, converges in 66 steps vs envelope prediction 73, L0=1.431, w0=(-3.78,-0.45). Verified against an independent Python implementation (mulberry32+Box-Muller, same update): L0, ratio factors, actual steps (66; kappa1/eta1:1; 1/1.8:31; 9/1.8:31; 20/1.0:120; 20/0.5:243; 100/1.8:299; 1000/1.8:2386; 20/2.05 diverges at 141; kappa1 eta0.01: 688 vs pred 687; kappa1000 eta0.01: pred 690,772, actual 429,844), predicted steps, noise floors (0.0681/0.0264/0.0046 at eta 1/0.5/0.1) and with noise the mean L over steps 201-300 (kappa1000 eta1.8 sigma.3: 0.4056 vs floor 0.4455; kappa1 eta1 sigma.3: 0.08164 vs 0.09) and L at step 300 all match to display rounding. widget-test en and zh: no errors, all 7 controls change output.
changes: slider value now sits beside its label (it previously dropped below the tick marks)
kappa slider value renders lambda_min with a real subscript
bars canvas taller; the 'stable only below 1' note no longer overlaps the axis ticks; right margin widened so '= rho' is not clipped at 400 px
num() no longer prints 6.611e+4 style numbers for values between 1e4 and 1e5
noisy run that diverges now reports 'infinity (diverges at step n)' instead of 'not measured with noise'
'first 300 steps shown' reworded to 'plots show the first 300 steps' (the actual step count can exceed 300)
issues: The spec's extra stop rule '||w|| > 10^3' was deliberately not implemented: it makes kappa=20 eta=2.05 diverge at step 134, contradicting the spec's reference value of 141 (L > 10^6 alone gives 141). Any state reaching ||w||>1000 has L>10^6 for the steep direction anyway.

Slider positions are on an integer 0-1000 scale with 3-significant-figure rounding, so exactly eta=2 is reachable (position 960) but values like 1.8 are only reached exactly through the presets; the marginal status was verified at eta=2.00.

In noisy runs the 'at the noise floor' status is judged from the noise-free part of the loss only, so for very large kappa it can read 'at the floor' while the running mean is still approaching the floor (kappa=1000, eta=1.8, sigma=0.3: mean 0.406 vs floor 0.446).
